subject.title: boot-md hook re-runs BOOT.md on every gateway restart

question: Should boot-md keep the documented per-gateway-startup BOOT.md behavior, switch to run-once per workspace/config generation, or split startup checks from first-run initialization?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs implement per-startup behavior, while the issue asks for a lifecycle change that needs canonical state ownership and reset semantics before code should change.

options.title: Make BOOT.md run-once with canonical state
options.body: Store completion/reset state in OpenClaw-owned state, keep boot sessions isolated, and update docs/tests so heavy first-run work cannot repeat on every restart.

options.title: Keep per-startup semantics
options.body: Document BOOT.md as a startup checklist and steer users toward idempotent content or disabling boot-md when repeated work is harmful.

options.title: Split first-run and startup hooks
options.body: Introduce a separate first-run initialization surface while leaving BOOT.md as the existing per-startup hook, at the cost of a broader design change.

recommendation.title: Make BOOT.md run-once with canonical state
recommendation.body: Store completion/reset state in OpenClaw-owned state, keep boot sessions isolated, and update docs/tests so heavy first-run work cannot repeat on every restart.

likelyOwner.reason: ngutman introduced the boot-md startup hook and is the clearest history-backed owner for deciding whether its original lifecycle should change.
